plan_deviations_observed.task: Task 4 — src/index.ts: correct video Content-Type, Accept-Ranges, and 416
plan_deviations_observed.plan_claim: Task 4 says to implement the 416-on-unsatisfiable-range behavior by reusing createR2Response's existing R2-native range math (the offset/length/suffix logic fed by getR2GetOptionsFromRequest -> BUCKET.get(key, {range})), via either an opts flag on createR2Response (option a) or a createVideoResponse that reuses the same offset/length/suffix math from createR2Response (option b). Both options assume the object is fetched WITH the client Range forwarded to R2, and that an out-of-bounds range can be detected from object.range so the path can return 416 instead of the image path's current 'fall back to 200'.
plan_deviations_observed.actual_finding: Empirically probed R2 in the @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers (Miniflare/workerd) runtime: BUCKET.get(key, {range}) with an out-of-bounds Range header 'bytes=99999-100000' against an 8-byte object does NOT return null and does NOT throw; it SILENTLY CLAMPS the range, returning the object with range={offset:0,length:8} (the full object). Probe output: 'PROBE_RESULT: OBJECT size=8 range={"offset":0,"length":8}'. Consequently the plan's R2-native-range math would compute start=0,end=7 and emit a 206 with the full body for an unsatisfiable range — it can never produce the 416 that Task 4 itself requires. (A secondary note: this also refutes a naive assumption that an unsatisfiable ranged get would 404 via findSourceImage's null guard; R2 instead clamps.)
plan_deviations_observed.fix_applied: For the video serve path, do NOT forward the Range header to R2. In handleImageRequest the video branch fetches the full object via findSourceImage(imageRequest, /* no getOptions */ undefined). A new createVideoResponse(object, request, contentType) parses the client's Range header manually against the authoritative object.size (object.size is the full size even on ranged gets) using a dedicated parseRangeHeader() helper that supports bytes=start-end, bytes=start-, and bytes=-suffix. It returns: 200 (full body stream) when no/invalid Range; 206 (arrayBuffer slice) with Content-Range/Content-Length for satisfiable ranges; and 416 with 'Content-Range: bytes */{size}' for well-formed-but-unsatisfiable ranges (start>=size, end<start, or suffix=0). Content-Type is overridden with VIDEO_CONTENT_TYPES[ext] and Accept-Ranges: bytes is set on both 200 and 206. This satisfies every Task 4 / Section-4 assertion (content-type override, full-200 Accept-Ranges, 206 bounded/open-ended/suffix, 416 with bytes */{size}, 405 non-GET) which the plan's prescribed native-range mechanism could not.
plan_deviations_observed.discovered_via: Wrote a temporary probe spec (test/_probe.spec.ts) that seeded an 8-byte R2 object and called env.BUCKET.get(key, {range: Headers{Range: 'bytes=99999-100000'}}) inside the cloudflare:test worker runtime, logged the result, then removed the probe. Confirmed clamping behavior before finalizing createVideoResponse.
